migrationCompatibility.notes: No migration is added, removed or altered in what it DOES. One down_revision pointer moves, which changes only the order Alembic applies existing migrations in. Production is at 043_stop_reason_consent_pause, precisely the revision the W7 chain now descends from, so the chain applies forward with no rewrite of applied history.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: redeploy the prior release. Note the asymmetry: if 043_juli_app_role..047 have already been applied, reverting this branch restores the two-head state and `alembic upgrade head` aborts again — the forward fix, not a revert, is the recovery.

acceptanceCommands: PYTHONPATH=$PWD/backend/src python -m pytest tests -m 'not live and not demo_contract' -q
doNotInfer: Do not renumber 043_juli_app_role..047 to 044..048. Their revision ids are referenced from fourteen files including the committed status records for #1326 and #1328, which are the merge-time source of truth under ADR-003. Filename ordering is cosmetic; the ids are what Alembic reads.

Do not relax an assertion in test_agent_adversarial_loop_behaviour.py to make it pass. It is a security corpus. Every change must name the runner-semantics cause and be justified against observed behaviour.

Do not treat the stop_reason divergence on hidden_text_homoglyph_lookalike as an attack succeeding. The inbound guard blocks the payload, so the required step is not credited and the run does strictly LESS than the benign one.

Do not hand-write agent-runtime/artifacts/status/issue-1403.json. Generate it with generate_status_records.py — the guard is fail-closed on schema and a hand-written record fails CI while reading PASS.
Do not add register_terminal_tools only where a test happens to fail. ADR-088 resolves TerminationPolicy.terminal_tools against whichever registry is passed, so every hand-rolled registry needs it.
